material_systems.name: Acrylic Stain-Blocking Spot Primer

primer.type: Acrylic stain-blocking primer for spot-priming bare areas
products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Latex Primer
primer.notes: For spot-priming bare areas on otherwise sound existing paint. Coverage based on affected area, not total wall SF. Apply to all exposed bare wood after scraping and sanding.

material_systems.notes: Spot prime only — not full-surface prime. Used on sound_paint (minor touch-ups) and failing_paint with less than 30% bare exposure. Coverage is per affected area.

material_systems.name: Chalk-Binding Conditioner Primer

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Multi-Purpose Primer
primer.notes: Low-viscosity, high-penetration formula binds loose chalk residue and creates sound adhesion base. Must be applied after power washing and drying. Higher material consumption due to chalk absorption.

material_systems.notes: REQUIRED for chalking surfaces. Penetrates and binds loose chalk particles. Do not skip — topcoat adhesion failure guaranteed without this step.

material_systems.name: Acrylic Stain-Blocking Full Primer

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
primer.notes: Full-surface primer for extensive bare wood exposure after scraping. Standard softwoods (pine, fir, spruce). For tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood), use SYS_EXT_WSRP_PRIMER_STAIN_BLOCK_ALKYD instead.

material_systems.notes: Full prime for failing (>30% bare) and peeling states on standard softwoods. If tannin-rich wood is exposed, switch to alkyd stain-blocker.

material_systems.name: Alkyd Stain-Blocking Primer

products: KILZ Original Multi-Surface Stain Blocking Primer
primer.notes: REQUIRED for tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood) with bare wood exposed. Oil-based provides superior tannin bleed block vs. acrylic. Longer dry time — 24 hr recoat in cool weather. VOC restrictions may apply in some jurisdictions.

material_systems.notes: Tannin-rich species override. When cedar/redwood bare wood is exposed on failing, peeling, or weathered states, this system replaces the acrylic primer. Higher material consumption due to absorptive grain.

material_systems.name: Deep-Penetrating Oil-Alkyd Primer

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start All-Purpose Alkyd Primer
primer.notes: For fully weathered bare wood with loose surface fibers. Deep penetration binds deteriorated wood fibers and provides sound film foundation. Highest material consumption of any primer — weathered wood absorbs aggressively.

material_systems.notes: REQUIRED for weathered bare wood. Penetrating formula consolidates loose fibers. Do not substitute acrylic — insufficient penetration for weathered substrate.

material_systems.name: Exterior Acrylic Latex Siding Paint

finish.notes: QT2 economy repaint — single finish coat over primed/sound surface. Acceptable for rental/turnover properties. 2 coats strongly recommended for improved durability and coverage but not required at this tier.

material_systems.notes: QT2 single-coat finish. Provides acceptable appearance and weather protection. Shorter maintenance cycle than 2-coat system.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Latex

finish.notes: Standard production-grade 2-coat system. Good color retention, mildew resistance, and UV stability. Second coat ensures uniform color and full film build.

material_systems.notes: Standard exterior production system. 2 coats for full hide and proper film build.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Acrylic

finish.notes: Premium residential grade. Superior color retention, fade resistance, flexibility. Self-priming on previously painted surfaces in good condition. 2 coats required.

material_systems.notes: Premium exterior system. Better durability, longer maintenance cycle than standard.

spot_prime_area.notes: Coverage based on affected bare area, not total wall SF. Estimate bare percentage and multiply by wall area.

assumptions: Coverage applies to affected area only — not full wall SF.
Bare percentage typically 5-15% on sound_paint, 15-30% on mild failing_paint.

SS_EXT_CHALKING.notes: Full-surface application. Chalk residue absorbs significant primer. Heavy chalk = lower end of range.

assumptions: Full-surface coverage required — chalk binding must be uniform.
Power wash first to remove loose chalk; primer binds remaining residue.

SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT.notes: Mixed surface — some bare, some existing coating. Acrylic primer.

SS_EXT_PEELING.notes: Mostly bare after scraping. Acrylic primer for standard species.

tannin_rich_failing.notes: Alkyd primer on tannin-rich species. Lower coverage due to grain absorption.

tannin_rich_peeling.notes: Alkyd primer on tannin-rich, mostly bare. Highest consumption for full prime.

assumptions: Full-surface prime on failing (>30%) and peeling states.
Alkyd coverage 15-20% lower than acrylic due to tannin-rich wood absorption.

SS_EXT_WEATHERED.notes: Weathered bare wood absorbs aggressively. South/west exposures at lower end. Severely weathered may need 2 applications.

assumptions: Penetrating primer is absorbed into wood — minimal surface film build.
Severely deteriorated wood (soft, punky) = HARD STOP — outside painting scope.

lap_horizontal.notes: Smooth lap siding over primed surface. Standard coverage.

board_and_batten.notes: Effective area ~1.20x net due to batten profiles.

shingle.notes: Many edges, overlapping profiles. Highest material consumption.

textured_rough_sawn.notes: Rough texture increases material consumption ~15% vs smooth.

assumptions: Coverage is per NET siding area from PaintScope.
Repaint coverage slightly higher than new construction — primed/existing paint reduces absorption.
Two-coat system standard at QT3/QT4. Single coat at QT2.

consumables.name: Airless spray tips 515-617
consumables.notes: 515 tip for finish, 517 for primer. 617 for heavy-body primer on rough surfaces.

consumables.name: Roller covers 3/8-1/2 inch nap
consumables.notes: 3/8 inch nap for smooth siding, 1/2 inch for textured. Used for back-rolling after spray.

consumables.name: Brushes 3-4 inch for edges and detail
consumables.notes: 3 inch for detail/trim junction. 4 inch for field brush application.

consumables.name: Extension poles
consumables.notes: 4-8 ft extension pole for roller/brush work from ground or scaffold.

consumables.name: Carbide scrapers
consumables.notes: For removing loose and peeling paint. Carbide stays sharp longer than steel.

consumables.name: Paint shaver / power scraper (HEPA for RRP)
consumables.notes: Power paint removal tool. HEPA-equipped model required for pre-1978 homes under RRP rule.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 80-120 grit
consumables.notes: For feathering scraped edges and removing loose material.

consumables.name: Orbital sander pads 80-120 grit
consumables.notes: For orbital/random orbit sander. Faster than hand sanding on large areas.

consumables.name: TSP cleaner / degreaser
consumables.notes: Trisodium phosphate or TSP substitute for surface cleaning before painting. Mix per manufacturer directions.

consumables.name: Wood brightener / oxalic acid
consumables.notes: For weathered wood restoration. Removes gray oxidation and opens wood pores for primer penetration. Conditional — weathered state only.

consumables.name: Acrylic latex exterior caulk
consumables.notes: Paintable exterior caulk for joint replacement at butt joints, trim-to-siding, and corner boards.

consumables.name: Masking tape (exterior grade UV-resistant)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum.

consumables.name: Masking paper / kraft paper
consumables.notes: For masking windows, doors, and fixtures during spray application.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 4 mil
consumables.notes: For landscape, hardscape, and fixture protection during spray.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloths
consumables.notes: Reusable canvas drops along foundation for drip protection.

consumables.name: Lead test kits (EPA-recognized)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true. EPA-recognized test kits (e.g., 3M LeadCheck). Required before disturbing paint on pre-1978 structures.

consumables.name: Polyethylene sheeting 6 mil (RRP containment)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. 6-mil poly for ground containment extending 10 ft from structure per RRP rule.

consumables.name: HEPA vacuum bags
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. For HEPA vacuum during and after lead-safe scraping.

consumables.name: Lead-safe waste disposal bags
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. 6-mil bags for lead paint waste. Labeled per EPA requirements.

consumables.name: P100 respirator cartridges
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. P100 particulate filter for half-face respirator during lead paint disturbance.

consumables.name: Disposable coveralls (Tyvek)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. Disposable coveralls prevent lead dust transfer.

compatibility_rules.notes: Existing paint is sound. Spot-prime bare areas from minor scraping/sanding only.
MANDATORY. Topcoat will fail without chalk-binding step.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing paint >=30% bare, standard wood — full acrylic prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Extensive bare exposure on standard softwoods requires full prime.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing paint >=30% bare, tannin-rich wood — full alkyd prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Tannin-rich override. Cedar/redwood bare exposure requires alkyd stain-blocker.

compatibility_rules.description: Peeling, standard wood — full acrylic prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Peeling = extensive bare after scraping. Full prime required.

compatibility_rules.description: Peeling, tannin-rich wood — full alkyd prime
Weathered bare wood — penetrating primer required
compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY. Acrylic primer lacks penetration for weathered fiber structure.

compatibility_rules.description: Weathered + tannin-rich — penetrating primer then alkyd stain-block
compatibility_rules.notes: Weathered tannin-rich may require penetrating primer followed by tannin-blocking coat. Assess on-site.

then.reason: Structural wood damage outside painting scope. Refer to carpenter/contractor.

compatibility_rules.notes: Soft, punky, or structurally compromised wood cannot be painted. Requires replacement first.
Economy tier. Single coat acceptable but 2 coats recommended for durability.

compatibility_rules.description: Pre-1978 with paint disturbance — RRP supplies required
compatibility_rules.notes: EPA RRP Rule (40 CFR 745) requires lead-safe work practices for pre-1978 homes when disturbing >6 SF per room exterior or >20 SF total.
